verdict.rationale: Open WebUI supports programmatic, non-UI use. API keys let external code call the same endpoints the web UI uses, and the Computer gateway exposes workspaces as OpenAI-compatible models that any OpenAI-style client can use to run agent tasks. It also ships a minimal CLI (`cptr run`) and deploys via Docker or Kubernetes. However, the REST API is declared experimental with no deprecation window, and nothing documents CI integration or a headless run mode beyond calling a running server. Scheduled Automations are recurring in-app runs, not CI invocation, so they are not credited. missing for 10: documented CI/pipeline usage or examples, a stable non-experimental API, clear docs on what the `cptr run` CLI does for automation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: An API key is a personal access token that lets external code call the same endpoints the web UI uses.
The gateway exposes each of your workspaces as an OpenAI-compatible model, so any OpenAI-style client can run agent tasks in a real workspace.
The CLI has exactly one command: cptr run
